questions.question: The Ministry of Culture organized "Tiranga Utsav" on ________, 2022 to celebrate the contributions of Pingali Venkayya to the country.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2nd August**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Ministry of Culture organized the **Tiranga Utsav** to celebrate his contributions to the country.
 
• It is a national festival celebrated on **August 2nd every year** to **honor the national flag** and its **designer Pingali Venkayya.**
 
• The festival includes various cultural events, flag-hoisting ceremonies, and patriotic speeches.
 
• It also witnessed the release of **‘Amar Chitra Katha’ **in the memory of revolutionary Tribal fighters of Indian freedom struggle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **5th September** is celebrated as **Teachers' Day** in India in** honor of Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan.**
 
• **Pingali Venkayya:**
 
 
• He was a freedom fighter and the **designer of the Indian National Tricolour.**
 
• Born on August 2, 1876, in the Krishna district of Andhra Pradesh, Venkayya served in the British Army during the Anglo-Boer War in South Africa.
 
• In **1921**, he **met with Mahatma Gandhi** in Vijayawada and showed him his publication with the various designs of the flag.
 
• The **flag **was officially** adopted by the Indian National Congress **in **1931**.
 
• The **current design of the National Flag was adopted by the Constituent Assembly** of India on** 22 July 1947.**

questions.question: Who among the Mauryan ruler pioneered the propagation of Buddhism?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ashoka.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ashoka **was one of the most famous **Mauryan rulers** who ruled from** 268 to 232 BCE.**
 
• He is known for his conversion to Buddhism and his efforts to spread the religion throughout his empire.
 
• **After **a brutal **battle In Kalinga **in **261 BCE**, he became disillusioned with the violence and bloodshed that he had witnessed.
 
• He **turned to Buddhism** as a way to find inner peace and to promote nonviolence and compassion.
 
• He issued edicts that promoted religious tolerance, urged his subjects to follow the principles of Buddhism, and built monuments and shrines to honor the Buddha.
 
• He **sent missionaries** to neighboring kingdoms and even as far as **Greece** and **Egypt**.
 
• He also convened the famous** Third Buddhist Council** in** 250 BC** at **Pataliputra, Bihar,** which helped to codify the teachings of the Buddha and to promote a more unified Buddhist community.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Samparti **was 5th ruler of the Mauryan Empire and the** ****grandson of Ashoka.**

 
 
• He is regarded for his **patronage and efforts to spread Jainism** in East India.
 
 
 
• **Devavarman **7th Emperor of the Maurya Empire.
 
 
• He **patronized Hinduism**.
 
 
 
• **Bindusara **was the** father of Ashoka** and the son of the **dynasty's founder Chandragupta Maurya.**
 
 
• The Buddhist texts **Samantapasadika** and **Mahavamsa **suggest that **he followed Brahmanism**.

questions.question: Licensing policy of the government was primarily aimed to promote _______ .

options.text: development of schools and hospitals in smaller states
growth of textiles in southern part of India

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**regional equality.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The licensing policy** of the government was introduced **to regulate the industrial sector** and **ensure fair competition among businesses**. It aimed to control the establishment, expansion, and operation of industries through a licensing system.
 
• The **primary objective of the licensing policy was to promote regional equality** and** balanced economic development across different states** and regions of the country.
 
• It sought to prevent the concentration of industries in a few regions and encourage their dispersal in less-developed areas.
 
• Another objective of the licensing policy was to** promote import substitution and self-reliance in the economy.**
 
 
• It encouraged the production of goods and services within the country and discouraged their importation from abroad.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**** Licensing Policy in India:**

 
• **Industrial licensing in India** is a mandatory rule put forth by the government of India for enterprises belonging to certain industries. 
 
• The licensing policy was **introduced in the Industrial Policy Resolution(IPR) of 1956** to **promote regional equality.**
 
• The rule was passed under the **Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, of 1951**, also known as IDR Act.
 
• Under this policy, private entrepreneurs were required to obtain a government license before establishing a new industry or expanding an existing one.
 
• It also aimed to protect the interests of small-scale industries and prevent the domination of large corporations.
 
• It had **some drawbacks** too as
 
 
• Bureaucratic delays, corruption, and rent-seeking behavior among officials and businessmen were caused by it.
 
• It also stifled innovation and efficiency in the industrial sector by creating entry barriers and limiting competition.

questions.question: _______ is an example of plastic money.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __** Credit card**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Plastic money** refers to the use of plastic cards, usually credit or debit cards, as **a medium of exchange instead of physical cash**.
 
• **Credit cards** are a common **example of plastic money**, as they allow users to make purchases without carrying physical currency.
 
• They are widely accepted and often come with rewards or cashback programs, making them a popular choice for many consumers.
 
• While credit cards can be convenient, it's important to use them responsibly and pay off balances in full to avoid accumulating debt.
 
• It's important to be aware of potential fraud or identity theft risks associated with credit cards and other forms of digital payment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Legal tender** refers to any form of **currency that is recognized as valid by a government or financial system**.

 
 
• This can include physical **cash or coins**, as well as** digital currencies like Bitcoin**.
 
 
 
• **Hard cash** refers specifically to **physical currency**, such as **coins, banknotes or** **bills**.
 
• **Coins **are a type of** physical currency** that is typically** made of metal** and used for smaller transactions.

questions.question:
What best defines prokaryotic cells?

I. Single chromosome

II. Membrane-bound cell organelles absent
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Prokaryotic cells** are** unicellular organisms** that **lack a nucleus and other membrane-bound organelles** in their cytoplasm.
 
• The genetic material of prokaryotic cells is present in a **single circular chromosome** that is** not enclosed within a membrane**.
 
• They are generally smaller in size than eukaryotic cells and have a simpler structure.
 
• They are found in **bacteria **and **archaea**, which are two of the three domains of life on Earth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Eukaryotic **and **Prokaryotic** cells are the two main types of cells that make up living organisms.
 
• Here are the key differences between them:

 
 

 **Part**
 **Eukaryotic cells**
 **Prokaryotic cells**
 
 

 **Nucleus**
 have a true nucleus, their genetic material is enclosed within a membrane-bound nucleus.
 lack a true nucleus, genetic material is present in a region called the nucleoid, which is not enclosed by a membrane.
 
 

 Membrane-bound organelles
 have membrane-bound organelles such as mitochondria, endoplasmic reticulum, and Golgi apparatus.
 lack membrane-bound organelles.
 
 

 **Chromosomes**
 most have multiple linear chromosomes.
 have just one circular chromosome.
 
 

 Reproduction
 by **mitosis **(for somatic cells) or **meiosis **(for sex cells).
 by **binary fission**.
 
 

 DNA Structure
 Linear DNA is complexed with histone proteins, present in the nucleus.
 Circular DNA is found in the nucleoid region, without histone proteins.
 
 

 **Examples**
 plants, animals, fungi, and protists.
 bacteria and archaea.

questions.question: As of November 2022, who among the following is the Governor of Kerala, India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arif Mohammed Khan.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As of November 2022, **Arif Mohammed Khan**__ is the** Governor of Kerala, India.**
 
• He is a former Member of Parliament and a former Cabinet Minister in the Government of India.
 
• He has held several portfolios ranging from energy to civil aviation
 
• He was appointed as the **22nd Governor of Kerala** in September 2019 and is **currently serving**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mangubhai Chaganbhai Patel**__ is the current Governor of Madhya Pradesh, appointed in September 2021.

 __
 
• He has earlier served as a cabinet minister in the Government of Gujarat.
 
 
 
• **Ganesh Lal Mathur **is a retired Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer who served as the **Chief Secretary of Rajasthan** and **retired **in 2010.
 
• **Bhagat Singh Koshyari** was the** 22nd Governor of Maharashtra** from 5 September 2019 to 17 February 2023
 
 
• He also served as the **2nd Chief Minister of Uttarakhand**.
 
 
 
• **Ramesh Bais** is the** current governor of Maharashtra** since February 18, 2023.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**The Governors of states:

 
• Governors have been discussed under Article 153 to Article 162 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The Governor is the constitutional head of a state in India and is responsible for the administration of the state.
 
• Under Article 155, the appointment of the Governor is done by the President of India by warrant under his hand and seal.
 
• He/She holds office at the pleasure of the President, which means that the President can remove the Governor from office at any time without assigning any reason.
 
• The term of governor's office is normally 5 years but it can be terminated earlier.
 
• He/She can also resign from his/her office by addressing the resignation letter to the President.
 
• Under Article 157, the qualifications for appointment as a Governor are: A Governor must
 
 
• be an Indian citizen and reside in the country.
 
• attain an age of a minimum of 35 years.
 
• not be a member of both houses of the parliament and the house of the state legislature.
 
• not hold any office for generating profit.

questions.question: Which of the following trophy is associated with women's Badminton?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uber Cup**__.

__
 
• **The Uber Cup** is a prestigious** international women's badminton tournament** that takes place **every two years.**
 
• It was **first held in 1956** and is **named after Betty Uber**, a former English badminton player who was instrumental in the development of the tournament.
 
• It is one of the oldest and most respected women's international team competitions in the world of sports.
 
• The tournament features teams from all over the world, with countries like China, Japan, Indonesia, and South Korea dominating the event over the years.
 
• So far, only five countries have won the Uber Cup with **China **the **most successful team**, with 15 titles.
 
• The **2022 edition** was held in **Bangkok**, **Thailand **in which** South Korea beat China** by **3-2**.
 
• 
 The next **edition of 2024** will be held in **Chengdu, China.**
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Davis Cup** is a **men's tennis tournament** that was **first **held in **1900**.

 
 
• It features national teams from around the world and is one of the most prestigious events in men's tennis.
 
 
 
• **Agha Khan Cup** is **a field hockey tournament** that takes place **in Pakistan.**
 
 
• It was **first **held in **1960 **and is named after the Aga Khan, the spiritual leader of the Ismaili Muslim community.
 
 
 
• **The FIFA World Cup** is a **men's football tournament** that takes place every four years.
 
 
• It features national teams from all over the world and is one of the most-watched sporting events on the planet.
 
• The** 2022 edition** was held in **Qatar**. **Argentina beat France** in **penalties **to win the tournament.
 
• The next **edition of 2026** is in **Canada**, **Mexico**, and **the United States**.

questions.question: Which railway station was awarded 'Eat Right Station' certification with a 4-star rating, in November 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhopal Junction Railway Station.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bhopal Railway Station** has been awarded a **4-star 'Eat Right Station' certification** for providing high-quality, nutritious food to passengers in November 2022.
 
• The station has received a **5-star rating indicating full compliance with safe and hygienic food regulations** for passengers.
 
• Other Railway Stations with this Certification: **Anand Vihar Terminal Railway Station(Delhi)**, **Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus(Mumbai)**, **Mumbai Central Railway Station, (Mumbai)**, **Vadodara Railway Station(Gujarat)**, and **Chandigarh Railway Station.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Eat Right Station certification** is a program launched **by **the **Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI)** in **2018 **to promote food safety and hygiene at railway stations.
 
• The certification is part of the **'Eat Right India' movement.**
 
• The certification is awarded to railway stations based on their compliance with food safety and hygiene standards, availability of healthy food options, and promotion of healthy eating habits among passengers.
 
• The certification has** five levels** - 1-star, 2-star, 3-star, and 4-star and 5-star with 5-star being the highest rating.

questions.question: A Khilafat Committee was formed in _______ in March 1919.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bombay.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Khilafat Committee **was **formed **in **Bombay**** **in **March 1919 **to **protest against the dismantling of the Ottoman Caliphate** in **Turkey **after World War I.
 
• The committee was led by prominent Muslim leaders such as **Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar** and his brother **Shaukat Ali**, and it gained widespread support from Muslims across India.
 
• The organization was **based in** **Lucknow.**
 
• The Khilafat movement, of which the committee was a part, played a significant role in the Indian independence movement, as it brought together Muslims and Hindus in a common cause against British colonialism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** **The Khilafat movement (1919–22):**

 
• Indian Muslims in British India launched a political campaign against British policies towards Turkey and the planned dismemberment of the Ottoman Empire by Allied forces after World War I.
 
• **Maulana Abul Kalam Azad**,** M.A. Ansari**, **Saifuddin Kitchlew** and the** Ali brothers** were the prominent leaders of this movement.
 
• The Khilafat Movement was closely associated with the Non-Cooperation Movement led by Mahatma Gandhi, creating a significant period of cooperation between Hindus and Muslims in the Indian nationalist struggle.
 
• In** November 1919**, **Mahatma Gandhi chaired a joint conference of Hindus and Muslims**, to unite both communities to gain independence for India.
 
• On **June 9, 1920**, the** Khilafat Committee in Allahabad** unanimously accepted the suggestion of non-cooperation and **asked Gandhi to lead the movement.**

questions.question: There is no requirement to maintain any minimum balance _______ in accounts.

• **Accident Insurance Cover of Rs.1 lakh** (enhanced to Rs. 2 lakh for new PMJDY accounts opened after 28.8.2018) is available with a RuPay card issued to the PMJDY account holders.
 
• An **overdraft (OD) facility up to Rs. 10,000** to eligible account holders is available.
 
• PMJDY accounts are eligible for Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT), Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY), Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY), Atal Pension Yojana (APY), Micro Units Development & Refinance Agency Bank (MUDRA) scheme.

questions.question: Which article of the Indian Constitution Deals with Matters relating to, or connected with, the election of a President or Vice-President?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**71.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 71** of the Constitution of India deals with **"Matters relating to, or connected with, the election of a President or Vice-President". **
 
• According to **Article 54**, The **President of India is elected by** an Electoral College consisting of the
 
 
• (a) **elected members of both Houses** of Parliament and of
 
• (b) **elected members of the Legislative Assemblies** of the States.
 
 
 
• The President is elected for a **term of five years** and is eligible for re-election.
 
• According to **Article 66**, The **Vice-President of India is elected by** an Electoral College consisting of the **members(elected and nominated) of both Houses of Parliament**.
 
 
• The Vice-President is also elected for a term of five years and can be re-elected.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 69** deals with the **Oath or affirmation by the Vice-President**.

 
 
• Every Vice-President shall, before entering upon his office, make and subscribe** before the President, or some person appointed on that behalf by him**, an oath or affirmation.
 
 
 
• **Article 70 **deals with the **Discharge of the President's functions in other contingencies**.
 
 
• Parliament may make such provision as it thinks fit for the discharge of the functions of the President in any contingency not provided for at another place.
 
 
 
• **Article 68** deals with the **Time of holding an election to fill vacancies in the office of Vice-President** and the term of office of the person elected to fill the casual vacancy.
 
 
• An election to fill a vacancy caused by the expiration of the term of office of Vice-President shall be completed before the expiration of the term.
 
• An election to fill a vacancy in the office of Vice-President occurring because of his death, resignation or removal, or otherwise shall be held as soon as possible after the occurrence of the vacancy, and the person elected to fill the vacancy shall, subject to the provisions of article 67, be entitled to hold office for the full term of five years from the date on which he enters upon his office.

questions.question: Who was awarded the Sangeet Natak Akademi award and the Tulsi Samman by the government of Madhya Pradesh for contributions in Folk and tribal Dance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arjun Singh Dhurwey.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Arjun Singh Dhurve**, a retired teacher from the **Dindori district of Madhya Pradesh**, is a folk dancer born on 12th August 1953.
 
• He was the first post-graduate degree holder from the **Baiga tribe**
 
• He is famous for popularising** Baiga folk songs and dance.**
 
• In this form of dance, performers wear animal masks such as peacocks, elephants, and horses.
 
• He was **awarded Tulsi Samman by the Madhya Pradesh Govt in 1993-94.**
 
 
• The Tulsi Samman is a literary award given by the government of Madhya Pradesh for excellence in Hindi literature.​
 
 
 
• In **2022**, the Indian Government awarded him the **Padma Shri** for his exceptional contributions to the field of art.
 
• He authored a **book **'**Baiga Geet: Baiga Janjaati ke Prachalit Paramparik Geet'** which was published in **2010**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 

 
• **Vempati Chinna Satyam** was a renowned **Kuchipudi dancer and choreographer** who received numerous awards for his contributions to Indian dance. He passed away in 2002.
 
• **Mahaboob Subhani** is a** folk artist from Telangana who specializes in the traditional art of shadow puppetry.** He has received several awards for his work, including the Sangeet Natak Akademi award in 2019.
 
• **Zia Mohiuddin Dagar **was a noted **musician and scholar of the Dhrupad style** of classical Indian music. He passed away in 2017.

 

Sangeet Natak Akademi:

 
• It is the apex body in the field of performing arts in the country and was **set up in 1953** for the preservation and promotion of the vast intangible heritage of India’s diverse culture expressed in forms of music, dance and drama.
 
• The **Chairman of the Akademi is appointed by the President of India** for a **term of five years.**
 
• Sangeet Natak Akademi is an **autonomous body of the Ministry of Culture**, Government of India.
 
• The** registered office** of the Akademi is at Rabindra Bhavan, **New Delhi.**
 
• The Sangeet Natak Akademi Awards are the highest national recognition conferred on practicing artists.

questions.question: The following duty 'A parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to his child or his ward' was added to the Fundamental Duties by which Constitutional Amendment Act?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**86th.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The duty "A parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to his child or his ward between the age of six and fourteen years" was added to the Fundamental Duties by the** 86th Constitutional Amendment Act 2002.**
 
• This **amendment **was passed in the year 2002 and it **made education a fundamental right for all children in the age group of 6-14 years.**
 
• The amendment also made it mandatory for the state to provide free and compulsory education to all children in this age group.
 
• The inclusion of this duty in the Fundamental Duties highlights the importance of education in the development of the nation and the role of parents and guardians in ensuring that their children receive education.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The Constitution was amended in** 2001** through the **85th Constitutional Amendment Act** to provide **promotion reservations for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes**. **Article 16 was modified** accordingly.
 
• The **84th Constitutional Amendment Act**, passed in **2001**, amended **Article 338** of the Constitution to establish a **National Commission for Scheduled Castes.**
 
• The** 83rd Constitutional Amendment Act, passed in 2000**, amended **Article 243D** of the Constitution to** reserve seats for women in Panchayats.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**** Fundamental Duties:**

 
• The **idea **of Fundamental Duties is** inspired by the Constitution of Russia.**
 
• The **Swaran Singh Committee recommended **Fundamental Duties in 1976, following the internal emergency of 1975-77.
 
• The **42nd Amendment Act of 1976 **added **Article 51A under Part-IV A** of the Indian Constitution consisting of **10 Fundamental Duties** for the citizens.
 
• The** 86th Amendment Act 2002** later added the **11th Fundamental Duty** to the list.
 
• Like the Directive Principles, the** duties are also non-justiciable.**

questions.question: Exports in excess of imports result in trade _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**surplus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When a **country exports more than it imports**, it **generates a surplus, **which means it has more foreign currency to spend than its trading partners.
 
• It occurs due to a high demand for goods from a certain country in the global market.
 
• A trade surplus also** implies that the country has a net inflow of its local currency** from the outside market.
 
• A trade surplus **can create employment and economic growth**, but **may also lead to higher prices and interest rates within an economy** as well as a more expensive currency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **A deficit is the opposite of a surplus.**

 
 
• **​**It occurs when a country imports more than it exports, which means it has to borrow money from its trading partners to pay for the difference. 
 
• This can lead to a decrease in the country's wealth and economic growth.
 
 
 
• **A zero budget** **means** that the **total amount of money spent by the government is equal to the total amount of money received.**
 
 
• This has nothing to do with trade surplus or deficit.
 
 
 
• **Liability **refers to the **amount of money that a company or a country owes** to others.

questions.question: What is the name given to the path along the Pacific Ocean characterized by active volcanoes and frequent earthquakes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ring of Fire.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Ring of Fire** is a **horseshoe-shaped area** in the **Pacific Ocean**, **spanning 40,000 km**, that is **known for its high volcanic and seismic activity.**
 
• It is **home to more than 75% of the world's active and dormant volcanoes** and **experiences about 90% of the world's earthquakes.**
 
• It is formed due to the movement of tectonic plates in the Earth's crust, which causes subduction zones where one plate slides beneath another.
 
 
• This process causes volcanic eruptions and earthquakes along the Ring of Fire.
 
 
 
• It is also home to** several active geothermal areas**, where hot springs, geysers, and fumaroles can be found.
 
 
• These geothermal areas are often used as sources of geothermal energy.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cape Horn** is a rocky headland located on the** southern tip of South America.**

 
 
• It is known for its treacherous waters and strong winds.
 
 
 
• **The Bermuda Triangle** is a region in the** western part of the North Atlantic Ocean**, known for several mysterious disappearances of ships and aircraft.
 
 
• However, there is no scientific evidence to support the claims of paranormal activity in the Bermuda Triangle.
 
 
 
• **Drake Passage** is a body of water that** separates South America from Antarctica**.
 
 
• It is known for its rough seas and strong winds.
